R-ops-2 (A dropped webhook is logged only at debug level, in free text, through console) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, capped), or hand failed deliveries to a queue that retries later. Scenario: a merchant endpoint that answers 503 for 30 seconds during a deploy, or refuses connections, gets its five attempts within a few hundred milliseconds, all fail, and the event is dropped — the retry gives no chance to recover from a short outage while hammering a struggling server. Retrying is safe (merchants deduplicate by `x-event-id`), so only the spacing is missing. Also stop retrying on a 4xx other than 408/429: a 400 or 410 will not succeed on a second try.
findings.title: Webhook retries fire back to back, with no backoff

findings.recommendation: Use the project's structured logger (`src/logger.ts`, as `src/events.ts` does) and log the final drop at `error` level with fields — eventId, event type, merchant id or URL host, last HTTP status or error, attempts — and log each failed attempt at `warn` with the same fields. Scenario: a merchant's endpoint returns 500 for every attempt; no attempt is logged at all, because only thrown errors reach the `catch` and a non-ok response falls through silently; the final drop goes to `console.debug`, which production log levels usually discard; `deliver` returns `false` and the listener ignores it. The merchant never receives the payment notification and the operator has no trace, no status and no count to see it. Consider a counter of delivered and dropped webhooks so a merchant-wide failure shows on a dashboard.
findings.title: A dropped webhook is logged only at debug level, in free text, through console

findings.recommendation: `publish` in `src/events.ts` awaits each listener in turn, so a merchant endpoint that hangs makes this listener take up to five 5-second timeouts (25 s, more once backoff is added) before the next listener runs and `publish` returns. Whether that stalls the payment service depends on how its caller awaits `publish`, which this change does not show. Prefer enqueueing the delivery (or not awaiting it, with its own error handling) so a slow merchant cannot delay settlement processing.
findings.title: Delivery runs inside the payment event publish, holding it up to 25 seconds
